The 'behaviour of components' axiom (2) is the new input for local rings with two components. Review (REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23): Assumption 5.4.1 (1)–(2) reworded as printed on p.78: the special-fibre point is the specialization of the generic points, and both special fibres have dimension dim S_∞ − l₀ − 1.

items.name: Automorphic components propagate through the special fibre
items.statement: Under Assumption 5.4.1, with Supp_{R_∞}(H^*(C_∞)) = Spec T_∞: (1) there is an irreducible component C_a ⊂ Spec R_∞ containing the automorphic point x with C_a ⊂ Spec T_∞; (2) if C_a ⊂ Spec T_∞ is an irreducible component of Spec R_∞ which contains x and C ⊂ Spec R_∞ is an irreducible component such that C ∩ Spec(R_∞/ϖ) and C_a ∩ Spec(R_∞/ϖ) contain generic points x_C, x_a generalizing to the same generic point x′ of Spec R′_∞, then C ⊂ Spec T_∞.
items.note: H^*(C_{∞,a_∞}) is concentrated in degree q₀ + l₀ and Cohen–Macaulay ([CG18, Lemma 6.2], as [ACC+18, Prop. 6.3.8]); lengths of complexes [ACC+18, Lemma 6.3.7] carried through R′_∞. PA.3 plans the support implication for derived Ihara avoidance in ACC+'s form; this component-wise version is imported by BCG+25. Review (REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23): part (2) requires C_a to contain x, as printed on p.78; added.

items.name: Support of patched cohomology at points of automorphic components
items.statement: Let C be an irreducible component of Spec R_∞ satisfying the hypothesis of prop-5-4-2(2) for some automorphic C_a, x ∈ C and y its contraction to S_∞. Then the support of H^*(C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/y)_y over Spec R_∞ contains x; if y is one-dimensional of characteristic 0, x lies in the support of H^*(C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/y)[1/p].
items.note: Tor spectral sequence, as [ACC+18, Cor. 6.3.9].

items.name: Cohomology of PGL₂ locally symmetric spaces at non-neat level
items.statement: For F imaginary CM, G = PGL_{2,F}, K = ∏K_v ⊂ PGL₂(Ô_F) (not necessarily neat), S ⊇ S_p with K_v = PGL₂(O_{F_v}) for v ∉ S, R = O or O/ϖ^m and V an R[K_S]-module finite free over R with V/ϖ^r smooth: C•(K,V) := lim_r RΓ(K, RΓ(𝔛_G, V/ϖ^r)) ∈ D⁺(R) and C•(K/K′,V) ∈ D⁺(R[K/K′]) for open normal K′ with K′^S = K^S, with H(G^S,K^S)-actions (T_{v,i} images of GL₂ operators, T_{v,2} = 1, P_v(X)); RΓ(K/K′, C•(K/K′,V)) = C•(K,V); cohomology finitely generated, Hecke algebras T^S_G(C•(K/K′,V)) O-finite, localizations cut out by idempotents e_m.
items.note: Properties deduced from neat GL₂ level by [AKT23, §5, Lemmas 5.1, 5.2, Prop. 3.6].

items.name: Comparison with the Allen–Khare–Thorne complexes
items.statement: There are natural Hecke-equivariant quasi-isomorphisms A(K/K′, V) ≅ C•(K/K′, V), where A(K/K′, V) are the complexes of [AKT23, §5.1] built from singular chains of 𝔛̄^{dis}_G.

items.name: Galois representations for PGL₂ over CM fields
items.statement: Suppose p is odd, S = S^c, F contains an imaginary quadratic field and every finite v ∉ S of residue characteristic l has: S contains no l-adic place and l unramified in F, or l splits in an imaginary quadratic subfield of F. Then for every maximal m ⊂ T^S_G(C•(K/K′,V)) there is a continuous semisimple ρ̄_m : G_{F,S} → GL₂(T^S_G(C•(K/K′,V))/m) with det(X − ρ̄_m(Frob_v)) = P_v(X) mod m for v ∉ S; if ρ̄_m is absolutely irreducible there are N depending only on [F : Q], J with J^N = 0 and ρ_m : G_{F,S} → GL₂(T^S_G(C•(K/K′,V))/J) with det(X − ρ_m(Frob_v)) = P_v(X) mod J for v ∉ S; in particular det ρ_m = ε^{−1}_p.
items.note: Essentially [AKT23, Cor. 5.7] (K/K′ abelian unnecessary), reducing to neat GL₂ level ([AKT23, Cor. 5.5, Thms. 5.6, 5.8]) and [ACC+18, Thms. 2.3.5, 2.3.7].

items.name: Vanishing above the real dimension and perfectness
items.statement: Let m ⊂ T^S_G(C•(K,V)) be maximal with residue field k; assume V ⊗ k ≅ k with trivial K_S-action, p odd with ρ̄_m absolutely irreducible, and ζ_p ∈ F. Then H^i(C•(K,V))_m = 0 for i > dim_R X_G; in particular C•(K,V)_m is a perfect complex of R-modules.

items.name: The data and hypotheses (1)–(15) of the special case of Theorem 5.2
items.statement: Data: F imaginary CM, p odd, ι : Q̄_p ≅ C; S ⊇ S_p finite; R ⊂ S prime to p and S_p = S^cr_p ⊔ S^st_p; π cuspidal on PGL₂(𝔸_F), regular algebraic of weight 0. Hypotheses: (5) every prime below S or ramified in F splits in an imaginary quadratic subfield of F (so S is split over F⁺ and F/F⁺ unramified); (6) for v ∈ S_p there is a p-adic v′ ≠ v̄ of F⁺ with Σ_{v″≠v̄,v′}[F⁺_{v″} : Q_p] > ½[F⁺ : Q], and the residue field of v̄ is bigger than F_p; (7) π_v unramified for v ∉ R ∪ S^st_p; (8) π^{Iw_v}_v ≠ 0 for v ∈ R ∪ S^st_p; (9) for v ∈ S^st_p, π is ι-ordinary of weight 0 at v and r_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} is non-crystalline ordinary; (10) ζ_p ∈ F if S = S_p ∪ R; (11) otherwise S − (S_p ∪ R) contains two places of distinct residue characteristics; (12) v ∉ R^c and H²(F_v, ad⁰r̄) = 0 for v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p); (13) r̄_{π,ι} decomposed generic with r̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} irreducible; (14) r̄_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} trivial for v ∈ S_p ∪ R; (15) the p = 5 projective-image condition.

items.name: Automorphy lifting in the special case
items.statement: With the data and hypotheses (1)–(15), let ρ : G_F → GL₂(Q̄_p) be continuous with (1) ρ̄ ≅ r̄_{π,ι} and det ρ = ε^{−1}_p; (2) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} Barsotti–Tate for v ∈ S^cr_p; (3) r_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} ordinary iff ρ|_{G_{F_v}} ordinary, for v ∈ S^cr_p; (4) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} a non-crystalline extension of ε^{−1}_p by the trivial character for v ∈ S^st_p; (5) ρ unramified at v ∉ S; (6) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} unipotently ramified for v ∈ R. Then ρ ≅ r_ι(Π) for a cuspidal Π of PGL₂(𝔸_F) of weight 0.
items.note: Proof pp.82–85: levels K (Iwahori at R ∪ S^st_p, pro-v Iwahori at S − (S_p ∪ R)), parabolics Q_{v̄} of type (2,1,1)/B₄/Siegel for the cases cr-ord/ord/cr, the problems 𝒮_χ, prop-5-6-2, prop-5-6-3, lem-5-6-4, patching via [ACC+18, §6.4] and [AKT23, Prop. A.6] with χ = 1 and χ with χ_v² ≠ 1; Spec R′_∞ has 2^{|S_p|} components; prop-5-4-2 and cor-5-4-3 with prop-5-3-2, lem-5-3-3, lem-5-3-4 and [BLGHT11, Lemma 3.3]; [AKT23, Thm. 5.10].

items.name: The global deformation problems 𝒮_χ and 𝒮_{χ,Q}
items.statement: For χ = ∏_{v∈R} χ_v : ∏O^×_{F_v} → O^× trivial mod ϖ: 𝒮_χ = (ρ̄, ε^{−1}_p, S, {R^{ε^{−1},BT}_v}_{v∈S^cr_p} ∪ {R^△_v}_{v∈S^st_p} ∪ {R^{ε^{−1},χ_v}_v}_{v∈R} ∪ {R^{ε^{−1}}_v}_{v∈S−(S_p∪R)}), with the O[K_S]-module O(χ^{−1}) via Iw_v → O^×, (a b; c d) ↦ χ_v(a/d); for a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q,N,…) whose places have residue characteristic split in an imaginary quadratic subfield, 𝒮_{χ,Q} adds R^{ε^{−1}}_v for v ∈ Q, an O[Δ_Q]-algebra (Δ_v = k^×_v(p)).

items.name: Hecke-valued Galois representations satisfy the deformation problem 𝒮_χ
items.statement: There are N depending only on [F : Q], J ⊂ T^{S,Q_{S̄_p},S̄_p-ord}_G(C•(K, O(χ^{−1}))_m) with J^N = 0 and a continuous surjection f_{𝒮_χ} : R_{𝒮_χ} → T^{S,Q_{S̄_p},S̄_p-ord}_G(C•(K, O(χ^{−1}))_m)/J with char(f_{𝒮_χ} ∘ ρ^{univ}_{𝒮_χ}(Frob_v)) the image of P_v(X) for v ∉ S.
items.note: prop-5-5-2 away from S ∪ S^c; thm-4-2-15 at v ∈ S_p (after reduction to neat GL₂ level); [ACC+18, Prop. 6.5.3, Thm. 3.1.1] at the other places.

items.name: The same at Taylor–Wiles level
items.statement: There are N depending only on [F : Q], J ⊂ T_{χ,Q} with J^N = 0 and a continuous surjective O[Δ_Q]-algebra homomorphism f_{𝒮_{χ,Q}} : R_{𝒮_{χ,Q}} → T_{χ,Q}/J with char(f ∘ ρ^{univ}(Frob_v)) = P_v(X) for v ∉ S ∪ Q, where T_{χ,Q} is the image of T^{S∪Q,…}_G ⊗ O[Δ_Q] in End_{D(O[Δ_Q])}(C•(K₀(Q)/K₁(Q), O(χ^{−1}))_{n_Q}).
items.note: As prop-5-6-2 with [ACC+18, Thm. 3.1.1] for the O[Δ_Q]-linearity (cf. [ACC+18, Prop. 6.5.11], [AKT23, Prop. A.13]).

items.name: Patching complexes of homology
items.statement: C_{χ,Q} := RHom_{O[Δ_Q]}(C•(K₀(Q)/K₁(Q), O(χ^{−1}))_{n_Q}, O[Δ_Q]) is a perfect complex of O[Δ_Q]-modules with a canonical isomorphism C_{χ,Q} ⊗^L_{O[Δ_Q]} O ≅ C_χ := RHom_O(C•(K, O(χ^{−1}))_m, O) in D(O).
items.note: Duals of perfect complexes computing localized equivariant homology ([AKT23, Thm. 5.11]).

items.name: A reducibility criterion for mod-p representations (variant of DDT 4.11)
items.statement: Corrected statement (source issue E12): let G be finite, p odd, ρ : G → GL₂(F̄_p) with det ρ of order d > 1, and suppose (tr ρ(g))² = (1 + det ρ(g))² whenever det ρ(g) ≠ 1. Then ρ|_{ker(det ρ)} is reducible, unless d = 3 and the projective image of ρ is A₄; in that case ρ|_{ker(det ρ)} has projective image Z/2 × Z/2 and is absolutely irreducible. (Printed: the conclusion without the exception.)
items.note: [DDT97, Lemma 4.11] except d = 3; then Z ⊂ ker det ρ, the projective image surjects to C_d, and by Dickson ρ is reducible or the projective image is A₄, whose Klein four subgroup gives reducibility on ker det ρ. Review (REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23): the printed lemma is false for d = 3 (E12): G = SL₂(F₃) ≅ 2T ⊂ SL₂(F̄_p), p ≥ 5, twisted by a cubic character through 2T → C₃ satisfies (5.6.1), while ker det ρ = Q₈ acts irreducibly. The d ≠ 3 cases ([DDT97, Lemma 4.11]) stand.

items.name: Reduction of Theorem 5.2 to Proposition 5.6.1 by solvable base change
items.statement: Theorem 5.2 follows from prop-5-6-1: choose a finite set V of auxiliary places as in the proof of [AKT23, Thm. A.14]; a solvable Galois CM extension F₀/F in which V splits, π_{F₀} has Iwahori-fixed vectors everywhere, bad places become unipotent with q_w ≡ 1 mod p and trivial ρ̄, every p-adic place of F₀⁺ splits with residue field bigger than F_p and the degree condition holds, potentially crystalline places become crystalline with π unramified (and r_ι(π) crystalline by thm-4-3-1, ordinary iff ρ is), and non-potentially-crystalline places become non-crystalline extensions of ε^{−1}_p by 1; a further composite F₁ with three imaginary quadratic fields; if ζ_p ∉ F, two auxiliary degree-one places v₀, v₀′ from lem-5-6-5 and Chebotarev; then solvable descent [ACC+18, Prop. 6.5.13].
items.locator: End of the proof of Theorem 5.2, pp.85–87
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23): the choice of v₀, v₀′ with H²(F_{1,v₀}, ad⁰ρ̄) = 0 rests on Lemma 5.6.5, which fails when [F₁(ζ_p) : F₁] = 3 and ρ̄ has projective image A₄ (possible only for p ≡ 1 mod 3; E12). In that case every unramified Frobenius has eigenvalue ratio det^{±1} or q_v ≡ 1 mod p, so no such place exists and the printed proof does not cover it. The applications use p ∈ {3, 5}, where d divides 2 or 4, so Theorems 6.1, 7.1, 1.1 and 1.2 are unaffected.

items.name: Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary CM fields with good mod 3 or mod 5 image
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM field with ζ₅ ∉ F and E/F an elliptic curve such that (1) r̄_{E,3} is decomposed generic and r̄_{E,3}|_{G_{F(ζ₃)}} is absolutely irreducible, or (2) r̄_{E,5} is decomposed generic and r̄_{E,5}|_{G_{F(ζ₅)}} is absolutely irreducible. Then E is modular.
items.note: Proof p.90: prop-6-1-5/prop-6-1-6 with S^ord_p, S^ss_p, S^st_p the places of potentially good ordinary, potentially good supersingular and potentially multiplicative reduction give L/F solvable and a modular A/L with r̄_{E,p}|_{G_L} ≅ r̄_{A,p}; thm-5-2 applies to r^∨_{E,p}|_{G_L} (lem-6-1-7, lem-6-1-4); solvable descent.

items.name: Modularity over imaginary quadratic fields with irreducible mod 3 or mod 5 image over F(ζ_p)
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary quadratic field and E/F an elliptic curve with r̄_{E,3}|_{G_{F(ζ₃)}} or r̄_{E,5}|_{G_{F(ζ₅)}} absolutely irreducible. Then E is modular.
items.note: thm-6-1 and lem-6-2-2. (Printed 'Them E is modular'.)

items.name: Density-one modularity over Galois imaginary CM fields
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM field, Galois over Q, with ζ₅ ∉ F. Then 100% of Weierstrass equations over F, ordered by height, define a modular elliptic curve.
items.note: If F/Q is Galois and the image of r̄_{E,5} contains SL₂(F₅), then r̄_{E,5} is decomposed generic [AN20, Lemma 2.3] and r̄_{E,5}|_{G_{F(ζ₅)}} is absolutely irreducible; 100% of curves have such image by quantitative Hilbert irreducibility [Zyw10, Prop. 5.2].

items.name: Properties of the automorphic representation of a modular elliptic curve
items.statement: Let F be CM and E/F modular without CM, with r_{π,ι} ≅ r^∨_{E,p} for some p and ι. Then (1) π has trivial central character and weight 0 and is determined by E; (2) r_{π,ι} ≅ r^∨_{E,p} for every p and ι; (3) WD(r^∨_{E,p}|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T_{F_v}(π_v) for every ι and finite v ∤ p; (4) if E has potentially multiplicative reduction at v | p, π is ι-ordinary of weight 0 at v for every ι.
items.note: (1)–(3) [AKT23, Lemma 9.1] (via Varma [Var24]); (4) as [AKT23, Cor. 9.2]: π_v is a quadratic twist of Steinberg, ordinary by the proof of [Ger19, Lemma 5.6].

items.name: The projective mod-5 field avoids ζ₅
items.statement: Let F be CM with ζ₅ ∉ F and E/F with the projective image of r̄_{E,5}(G_{F(ζ₅)}) conjugate to PSL₂(F₅). Then the extension of F cut out by the projective image of r̄_{E,5}(G_F) does not contain ζ₅.
items.note: From the proof of [AKT23, Cor. 9.14]: r̄_{E,5}(G_{F(ζ₅)}) = SL₂(F₅); compare [G : H] with [F(ζ₅) : F] according to the order 2 or 4 of det. Review (REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23): moved from route 2 to route 8, a source for ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4 ('finite-subgroup facts of GL₂/PGL₂ … behaviour under restriction to cyclotomic fields'), as the accepted ACC+ item 300.

items.name: Mod-5 switching with prescribed reduction types at 5
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM field and ρ̄ : G_F → GL₂(F₅) continuous with determinant ε̄₅ and decomposed generic; S₅ = S^st₅ ⊔ S^ord₅ ⊔ S^ss₅; F^avoid/F finite Galois. Then there are a solvable CM extension L/F and an elliptic curve E/L with (1) E modular; (2) L/F linearly disjoint from F^avoid/F; (3) for v | 5 of F and w | v of L, E_{L_w} has good ordinary reduction if v ∈ S^ord₅, good supersingular reduction if v ∈ S^ss₅, and (split) multiplicative reduction if v ∈ S^st₅; (4) ρ̄|_{G_L} ≅ r̄_{E,5}; (5) ρ̄|_{G_L} decomposed generic.
items.note: Variant of [AKT23, Prop. 9.13]: an L-point of Y_ρ̄ (open in P¹_F) avoiding a thin set ([Ser08, Thm. 3.5.3]) in prescribed w-adic opens by weak approximation, modular by [AKT23, Prop. 9.12]. The printed (3) writes E_{F_w} (source issue E4).

items.name: Mod-3 switching with prescribed reduction types at 3
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM field with ζ₅ ∉ F and ρ̄ : G_F → GL₂(F₃) continuous with determinant ε̄₃ and decomposed generic; S₃ = S^st₃ ⊔ S^ord₃ ⊔ S^ss₃; F^avoid/F finite Galois. Then there are a solvable CM L/F and E/L with (1) E modular; (2) L/F linearly disjoint from F^avoid; (3) for w | v | 3, E_{L_w} good ordinary, good supersingular or (split) multiplicative according as v ∈ S^ord₃, S^ss₃, S^st₃; (4) ρ̄|_{G_L} ≅ r̄_{E,3}; (5) ρ̄|_{G_L} decomposed generic.
items.note: Proved as [AKT23, Prop. 9.15]. The printed (3) writes E_{F_w} (source issue E4).

items.name: Local properties of the auxiliary automorphic representation
items.statement: For E produced by prop-6-1-5 or prop-6-1-6 with r^∨_{E,p} ≅ r_ι(π) (p = 5 or 3) and w | p of L over v of F: π is ι-ordinary at w if v ∈ S^st_p, and π_w is unramified if v ∈ S^ord_p ⊔ S^ss_p.
items.note: From lem-6-1-3.

items.name: Goursat’s lemma
items.statement: Let G₁, G₂ be finite groups and H ⊂ G₁ × G₂ a subgroup whose projections p_i : H → G_i are surjective. Then N_i := H ∩ G_i are normal in G_i and there is an isomorphism φ : G₁/N₁ ≅ G₂/N₂ with H = {(g₁,g₂) : φ(g₁N₁) = g₂N₂}.
items.note: Mathlib states it for arbitrary groups (Mathlib/GroupTheory/Goursat.lean:104), with the normal subgroups I.goursatFst, I.goursatSnd. Review (REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23): checked at Mathlib 082e2d3 (Mathlib/GroupTheory/Goursat.lean:85, 104): goursatFst = {g : (g,1) ∈ I} is the paper's H ∩ G₁, and the two lemmas give the graph description, for arbitrary groups.

items.name: Over quadratic fields, irreducibility over F(ζ_p) gives decomposed genericity
items.statement: Let F/Q be quadratic, p odd and ρ̄ : G_F → GL₂(F̄_p) with ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible. Then ρ̄ is decomposed generic.
items.note: Galois closure L̃ of the projective kernel field embeds Gal(L̃₁/F(ζ_p)) into a product of two copies of Gal(L₁/F(ζ_p)) with surjective projections; Goursat gives τ with both components non-identity of order prime to p (Dickson or [Ser72, Prop. 15]); a rational prime l with Frob_l = τ (Chebotarev) splits completely in F, l ≡ 1 mod p, and the Frobenius images are regular semisimple. Review (REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23): moved from route 2 to route 8, a source for ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4 ('finite-subgroup facts of GL₂/PGL₂ … behaviour under restriction to cyclotomic fields'), as the accepted ACC+ item 300.

items.name: Modularity over imaginary quadratic fields with irreducible mod 5 or suitable mod 3 action
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary quadratic field and E/F an elliptic curve such that either (1) G_F acts irreducibly (not necessarily absolutely) on E[5], or (2) G_F acts irreducibly on E[3] and its image in Aut(E[3]) is not the normalizer of a split Cartan subgroup. Then E is modular.
items.note: By thm-6-1 and lem-7-1-1 it remains to treat the imaginary quadratic points of X(ns3°,b5), X(b3,ns5), X(ns3°,ns5) and X(s3,ns5) (cor-7-2-5, cor-7-3-4, cor-7-4-6). Remark 1.3.2: the 3–7 switch of [FLHS15, §7] seems much harder over imaginary CM fields (points on a twist of the Klein quartic over solvable CM extensions), which is why the split-Cartan mod-3 case and the hypothesis on X₀(15) remain.

items.name: Images with absolutely reducible restriction to F(ζ_p)
items.statement: Let F be a number field and ρ̄ : G_F → GL₂(F_p) irreducible with determinant ε̄_p and ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} absolutely reducible. (1) ρ̄(G_F) lies in the normalizer of a Cartan subgroup. (2) If p = 3, ρ̄(G_F) is conjugate to C⁺_s(3) (normalizer of a split Cartan) or to a subgroup of C_ns(3) (a non-split Cartan). (3) If p = 5 and [F(ζ₅) : F] = 4, ρ̄(G_F) is conjugate to a subgroup of C⁺_ns(5).
items.note: [FLHS15, Lemma 2.2] and the proof of [FLHS15, Prop. 4.1(b)]. Review (REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23): moved from route 2 to route 8, a source for ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4 ('finite-subgroup facts of GL₂/PGL₂ … behaviour under restriction to cyclotomic fields'), as the accepted ACC+ item 300.

items.name: Modular curves X(H) and X(H₁,H₂) with Borel and Cartan level
items.statement: For H ⊂ GL₂(F_p) containing −I with det(H) = F^×_p, X(H)/Q is the modular curve with its j-map X(H) → X(1); for H_i ⊂ GL₂(F_{p_i}) (p₁ ≠ p₂), X(H₁,H₂) is the normalization of X(H₁) ×_{X(1)} X(H₂), with cusps over ∞; for a number field F its non-cuspidal F-points correspond to Q̄-isomorphism classes of (E, [η]), η : ∏F²_{p_i} ≅ ∏E[p_i](Q̄) up to H₁ × H₂, with η^{−1} r̄_{E,p_i}(G_F) η ⊂ H_i. b_p, s_p = C⁺_s(p), ns_p = C⁺_ns(p) are the Borel and the normalizers of split and non-split Cartans; s_p° = C_s(p), ns_p° = C_ns(p).
items.note: Notation of [FLHS15, §2.2]. Tau Ceti's ModularCurves roadmap plans Katz–Mazur Γ_H quotient problems and coarse moduli over Z[1/N], not these Cartan-level curves with explicit models. Review (REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23): Tau Ceti ModularCurves layer 9 (9A–9D) plans the affine quotients Y_H; layer 10 compactifies only diamond quotients, and ModularCurvesPartII R13.4a only full, Γ₁ and Γ₀ level. Stays missing.

items.name: Modularity when X₀(15)(F) is finite
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary quadratic field with X₀(15)(F) finite. Then every elliptic curve E/F is modular.
items.note: By thm-7-1 only F-points of X₀(15) = X(b3,b5) (15A1) and X(s3,b5) (15A3, isogenous) remain; non-CM E are determined up to quadratic twist; the only quadratic fields with torsion growth are Q(√−1) and Q(√5) for X₀(15) (y² = x(x+16)(x+25)) and Q(√5) for X(s3,b5) (y² = x(x+1)(x+16)) [Kwo97, Thm. 1]; the 8 new points over Q(√−1) reduce to LMFDB curve 4050.1-c3, modular by Faltings–Serre [DGP10, LMF22]. The second paragraph misnames the curve (source issue E5).

items.name: Explicit models of small modular curves
items.statement: (1) X(b3) ≅ P¹_Q with j = (x+27)(x+3)³/x. (2) X(b5) ≅ P¹_Q with j = (x²+250x+5⁵)³/x⁵, and w₅ : x ↦ 5³/x. (3) X(ns3) ≅ P¹_Q with j = x³. (4) X(ns5) ≅ P¹_Q with j = 5³x(2x+1)³(2x²+7x+8)³/(x²+x−1)⁵. (5) X(ns3,ns5) is an elliptic curve over Q isomorphic to 225A1, with X(ns3,ns5)(Q) ≅ Z. (6) X(s3) ≅ P¹_Q with j = 3³(x+1)³(x−3)³/x³.
items.note: [SZ17, Table 1], [McM04, Table 3], [Che99, Prop. 5.1, Cor. 6.3]; (5): the singular model x³ = 5³y(2y+1)³(2y²+7y+8)³/(y²+y−1)⁵ is birational to y² − y = x³ + 1 (Magma file ns3ns5-elliptic.m).

items.name: A model and Jacobian for X(ns3°, b5)
items.statement: (1) X(ns3°,b5) is the smooth genus-one curve C : y² = −3(x⁴ + 2x³ − x² + 10x + 25) in P(1,2,1). (2) w₅ acts on x-coordinates by x ↦ 5/x. (3) Jac C is isomorphic to 45A2, with Jac C(Q) ≅ Z/2 ⊕ Z/2.
items.note: X(ns3,b5) ≅ P¹ with j = (x⁶+250x³+5⁵)³/x¹⁵; the degree-two cover is ramified at the j = 1728 points cut out by x⁴+2x³−x²+10x+25 (not (x²−5x−25)², excluded since Q(√5) is real); the twist is Q(√−3), the field of definition of the cusps of X(ns3°); Jacobian by [AKM+01] and two-descent (Magma ns3ob5.m).

items.name: Special points and divisors on C over Q(√−3)
Rational divisor classes on C
items.statement: Pic⁰(C) (degree-0 rational divisors modulo linear equivalence) ≅ Z/2, generated by [0⁺ − ∞⁻].
items.note: Following [BF04]: Riemann–Roch bases {1, f_i} of L(D_i + ∞⁺ + ∞⁻) over Q(√−3); E₀ is equivalent to P + σ(P) for P = (1+2i : 3+6i : 1); for E₁, E₂ the conics α₀² + 3α₁² + 6α₁ + 15 = 0 and α₀² + 3α₁² + 6α₁ + 12 = 0 have no rational points (3-adically). Remark 7.2.3: E₀'s conic has the point (3,2).

items.name: Quadratic points on X(ns3°, b5)
items.statement: If P ∈ C(F) for a quadratic field F and P is not one of the two points at infinity, then x(P) ∈ Q or x(P)x(σ(P)) = 5, σ the non-trivial element of Gal(F/Q).

items.name: Elliptic curves from quadratic points of X(ns3°, b5) are modular
items.statement: Let F be a quadratic field and E/F the elliptic curve underlying an F-point of X(ns3°,b5). Then E is modular.
items.note: Either E has rational j-invariant (x(P) ∈ Q), or P maps to a Q-point of X(ns3,b5)/w₅, so E and E^σ are 5-isogenous and E is a Q-curve, hence modular (cf. [FLHS15, §12]).

items.name: A model and Jacobian for X(b3, ns5)
items.statement: (1) X(b3,ns5) has genus 2, with hyperelliptic model C : y² = 9x⁶ − 6x⁵ − 35x⁴ + 40x² + 12x − 8. (2) The hyperelliptic involution is the Atkin–Lehner involution w₃. (3) Jac(C)(Q) ≅ Z/2 ⊕ Z/10.
items.note: Magma IsHyperelliptic/SimplifiedModel (file b3ns5.m); w₃ has 6 fixed points (from C/O_{Q(√−3)} and C/Z[√−3], moduli description [KP16]) or Aut has order 2 [LSR21]; rank 0 by two-descent (MordellWeilGroupGenus2, Stoll [Sto01]); Jac(C)(F₇) ≅ Z/2 ⊕ Z/20 and Jac(C)(Q)[2] of order 4 bound the torsion.

items.name: Quadratic points on a genus-2 hyperelliptic curve
items.statement: Let P be a quadratic point of C with conjugate σ(P). Either (1) [P + σ(P)] = [D_∞] in Pic(C), and then P = (x, ±√f(x)) with x ∈ Q (f the defining sextic); or (2) [P + σ(P) − D_∞] ≠ 0 and P + σ(P) is the unique effective degree-2 divisor in its class.
items.note: [D_∞] is the canonical class with L(D_∞) = ⟨1,x⟩; Riemann–Roch.

items.name: Imaginary quadratic points on X(b3, ns5)
items.statement: If P ∈ C(F) for an imaginary quadratic field F and P is not at infinity, then x(P) ∈ Q, or F = Q(√−11) and, up to complex conjugation, P = ((−5+√−11)/6, ±(17−√−11)/6).
items.note: Inspect the 19 non-zero classes A ∈ Jac(C)(Q) with A + [D_∞] effective (Mumford representation): 9 with rational x, 2 at ∞, 2 on the Q(√−11) points, 6 real quadratic.

items.name: Elliptic curves from quadratic points of X(b3, ns5) are modular
items.statement: Let F be a quadratic field and E/F the elliptic curve underlying an F-point of X(b3,ns5). Then E is modular.
items.note: Points with x(P) ∈ Q satisfy σ(P) = w₃(P), so E is a Q-curve; the Q(√−11) points (related by conjugation and w₃) give LMFDB curve 8100.2-a2 over Q(√−11), whose mod-5 image is the full normalizer of a non-split Cartan, so cor-6-1-1 applies (also checked by Faltings–Serre in the LMFDB).

items.name: Box’s relative symmetric-square Chabauty set-up
items.statement: For X/Q smooth projective geometrically irreducible with Jacobian J and a degree-2 map π : X → C: primes p₁,…,p_r of good reduction for C and X; divisors D₁,…,D_n generating a finite-index subgroup G ⊂ J(Q) with φ : Zⁿ ↠ G; I ≥ 1 with I·J(Q) ⊂ G; a finite set L ⊂ X^{(2)}(Q) with base point ∞ ∈ L, L = L^pb ⊔ L^npb (pulled back from C(Q) or not); L^good_i ⊂ L the points where [Box21, Thm. 2.1] (unique in its residue class mod p_i) or, for x = π^*(P) with P ∈ C(Q), [Box21, Thm. 2.4] (every point of the residue class is pulled back) applies; ι(x) = I([x] − ∞) and its reductions ι_p : X^{(2)}(F_p) → J(F_p); M^bad_i := ι^{−1}_{p_i}(red_{p_i}(G)) − red_{p_i}(L^good_i).
items.note: Following [Box21, §2.4] and Siksek's relative symmetric power Chabauty [Sik09]. ED.4 plans classical Chabauty–Coleman and ED.5 the Mordell–Weil sieve with reduction maps from the Jacobian subgroup; neither names symmetric powers, so this is routed as a source for them. Review (REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23): changed from planned to missing: ED.4 plans classical Chabauty–Coleman on a curve with rank r < g and ED.5 the Mordell–Weil sieve; neither plans symmetric powers or the relative (bi-elliptic) version. It stays in route 3, which widens those layers.

items.name: Residue classes of good known points
items.statement: If x ∈ X^{(2)}(Q) and red_{p_i}(x) ∈ red_{p_i}(L^good_i) for at least one i, then x ∈ L ∪ π^*C(Q).
items.note: Immediate from the definition of L^good_i.

items.name: Relative Mordell–Weil sieve criterion (Box)
items.statement: If ∩_{i=1}^r red^{−1}_{p_i}(ι_{p_i}(M^bad_i)) ⊂ G is empty, then X^{(2)}(Q) = L ∪ π^*C(Q).
items.note: [Box21, Theorem 2.6]; each red^{−1}(ι(M^bad_i)) is a union of cosets of ker(red_{p_i}) in G.

items.name: Plane quartic models of X(ns3°, ns5) and X(s3, ns5)
items.statement: (1) X(ns3°,ns5) ≅ C₁ : 9x⁴+19x²y²+y⁴+9x³+19x²y+22xy²+2y³+10x²+22xy+13y²+7x+12y+11 = 0, with unique automorphism of order 2 over Q, w₁ : (x,y) ↦ (x, −y−1). (2) X(s3,ns5) ≅ C₂ : −x⁴+2x³y+x²y²+8x³+2x²y−2xy²−y³−3x²−3xy+3y²+2x−3y+1 = 0, with unique automorphism of order 2 over Q, w₂ : (x,y) ↦ ((3x+y+2)/(4x−2y+1), (8x+y−8)/(4x−2y+1)). (3) The Q(√−55)-points P₁ = ((1+√−55)/28, (27−√−55)/56) and P₂ = ((3−√−55)/4, (3+3√−55)/4) of C₂ have j-invariant −32768.
items.note: Singular models from y² = −3(x²+12x+144) for X(ns3°) and X(ns5), desingularized in Magma; automorphisms by AutomorphismGroupOfPlaneQuartic [LSR21]. Both curves are bi-elliptic over X(ns3,ns5) (files ns3ons5.m, s3ns5.m).

items.name: Mordell–Weil data for the bi-elliptic genus-3 curves
items.statement: (1) rk Jac C_i(Q) = rk Jac X(Q) = 1 for i = 1, 2 (X = X(ns3,ns5)). (2) Jac C₁(Q)_tors is isomorphic to a subgroup of Z/2 ⊕ Z/2, and Jac C₂(Q)_tors ≅ Z/2 ⊕ Z/10. (3) For a generator D of Jac X(Q) ≅ Z and G_i = ⟨π^*_i D⟩: 4·Jac C₁(Q) ⊂ 2G₁ and 10·Jac C₂(Q) ⊂ ⟨5G₁, Jac C₂(Q)[2]⟩.
items.note: Chen's isogeny ([dSE00, Thm. 2]): Jac C₁ ~ new part of J₀(225)/w₂₅ (newforms 225.2.a.b, c, e; curves 225c, 225a, 225d of ranks 0, 1, 0); Jac C₂ ~ 5-new part of J₀(225)/⟨w₉,w₂₅⟩ (225.2.a.c, 75.2.a.a, 75.2.a.b); [Box21, Prop. 3.1]; torsion from #Jac(F_p), p = 7, 11, 13, with explicit generators D₁ (order 10), D₂ (order 2). For C₂ the printed statement (and the proof of prop-7-4-5) writes 5G₁ ⊂ Jac C₁(Q) where G₂ is meant (source issue E9).

items.name: Quadratic points on X(ns3°, ns5) and X(s3, ns5)
items.statement: (1) For X = X(ns3°,ns5), C = X(ns3,ns5) and π the quotient: X^{(2)}(Q) = π^*C(Q). (2) For X = X(s3,ns5): there are eight conjugate pairs of quadratic points not mapping to C(Q); two are defined over an imaginary quadratic field, namely P₁, P₂ of prop-7-4-3.
items.note: (1) [Box21, Thm. 2.4] at p = 43 with L of 8 pulled-back divisors (red₄₃(G) cyclic of order 7); (2) Box's Mordell–Weil sieve at 11 and 43 with G = ⟨5G₁, Jac C₂(Q)[2]⟩, I = 10 and 16 non-pulled-back divisors in L; Box's code and Ozman–Siksek's point search.

items.name: Elliptic curves from these quadratic points are modular
items.statement: (1) If F is a quadratic field and E/F underlies an F-point of X(ns3°,ns5), E is modular. (2) If F is imaginary quadratic and E/F underlies an F-point of X(s3,ns5), E is modular.
items.note: All relevant points map to rational points of X(ns3,ns5), except P₁, P₂ over Q(√−55) and their conjugates, which have rational j-invariant.

items.name: Irreducible components of completed tensor products of local lifting rings
items.statement: Let A₁, …, A_r be complete local Noetherian O-algebras with residue field k, each O-flat and equidimensional, all of whose irreducible components (and those of their special fibres) are geometrically irreducible. Then the irreducible components of A₁ ⊗̂_O ⋯ ⊗̂_O A_r are exactly the Spec of the completed tensor products of irreducible components of the factors, and likewise for the special fibres ([BLGHT11, Lemma 3.3]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23: used to verify Assumption 5.4.1 for R_∞, R′_∞ and to compare C and C_a. Planned as for the accepted PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 item 122 (R03.6: 'supported on a specified union of components').

items.name: Solvable base change and descent of automorphy for GL₂ over CM fields
items.statement: Let F be a CM field, F′/F a finite solvable Galois extension of CM fields, and π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F). (1) There is a regular algebraic automorphic representation π_{F′} of GL_n(𝔸_{F′}), the base change, with r_ι(π_{F′}) ≅ r_ι(π)|_{G_{F′}}, cuspidal when r_ι(π)|_{G_{F′}} is irreducible. (2) If ρ : G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) is continuous with ρ|_{G_{F′}} irreducible and automorphic, then ρ is automorphic ([ACC+18, Prop. 6.5.13], after Arthur–Clozel).
items.locator: §5.6, end of the proof of Theorem 5.2, pp.86–87; proof of Theorem 6.1, p.90
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23. R17.4 plans 'cyclic and solvable base change … Iterate to solvable extensions' for GL₂; ML.5 holds ACC+ Proposition 6.5.13 (accepted ACC+ items 268, 269).

items.name: Taylor–Wiles data for GL₂ over CM fields without enormous image (Allen–Khare–Thorne)
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM field, p odd, and ρ̄ : G_F → GL₂(k) continuous with ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible and, if p = 5 and the projective image of ρ̄(G_{F(ζ₅)}) is PSL₂(F₅), the field cut out by the projective image of ρ̄ not containing ζ₅. Then for every N ≥ 1 there is a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q_N, (α_v)_{v∈Q_N}) of level N (Definition 5.3.5) of size q independent of N, killing the relevant dual Selmer group ([AKT23, Prop. A.6]), used with [ACC+18, §6.4] as in the proof of [AKT23, Thm. A.7].
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23. R04.5, G7 and PA.4 plan Taylor–Wiles primes under adequacy or enormous image; the p = 3, 5 images (SL₂(F₃), PSL₂(F₅)) that AKT23 treat are not planned. Routed with route 1.

routes.title: Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields, Part II: P-ordinary degree shifting, crystalline local–global compatibility and Barsotti–Tate lifting
routes.brief:
Starts where Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure) stops. PA.1 and PA.2 plan local–global compatibility at p for the torsion Galois representations of Scholze only in the Fontaine–Laffaille and Borel-ordinary cases of Allen et al. (ACC+); this Part II proves it in the crystalline and P-ordinary cases with p small and arbitrarily ramified, and the potentially Barsotti–Tate automorphy lifting theorem it enables, following §§2–5 of Caraiani–Newton, 'On the modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields', arXiv:2301.10509v3 (27 March 2025).

Final theorems, as the paper states them. (a) Theorem 4.2.15: F imaginary CM containing an imaginary quadratic field, p split in an imaginary quadratic subfield, T ⊇ S_p with T = T^c and every v ∉ T of residue characteristic ℓ either with no ℓ-adic place in T and ℓ unramified in F or ℓ split in an imaginary quadratic subfield; K ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) good, hyperspecial off T; distinct p-adic places v̄, v̄′ of F⁺ with Σ_{v̄″≠v̄,v̄′}[F⁺_{v̄″}:Q_p] ≥ ½[F⁺:Q]; λ dominant; a parabolic Q_{v̄} ⊂ P_{v̄} of type (cr-ord) partition (n,1,…,1), (ord) B_{2n} or (cr) the Siegel parabolic, K_{v̄} = 𝒬_{v̄} ∩ G(F⁺_{v̄}); m non-Eisenstein, ρ̄_m decomposed generic, [K ν(ϖ) K] ∉ m. Then there are N = N(n,[F⁺:Q]), J^N = 0 and ρ_m over T^{Q_{v̄},{v̄}-ord}(RΓ(X_K,V_λ)_m)/J with unramified characteristic polynomials P_v(X), such that R^□_{ρ̄_m|G_{F_v}} → T/J factors through R^{△,λ_ṽ} at ṽ and R^{cris,λ_ṽc} at ṽ^c (cr-ord), through R^{△,λ_v} (ord), or through R^{cris,λ_v} (cr); Corollary 4.2.16 with fixed determinant when p ∤ n. (b) Theorem 4.3.1: for F totally real or CM, π cuspidal regular algebraic of weight λ on GL_n(𝔸_F), v | p with π unramified at v and v^c, r_ι(π) irreducible and decomposed generic, r_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} and |_{G_{F_{v^c}}} are crystalline with labelled Hodge–Tate weights λ_{ιτ,n} < … < λ_{ιτ,1} + n − 1. (c) Theorem 5.2: potentially Barsotti–Tate automorphy lifting for ρ : G_F → GL₂(Q̄_p), F imaginary CM, p odd, det ρ = ε_p^{−1}, all labelled Hodge–Tate weights (0,1), ρ̄ decomposed generic with ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} irreducible, the p = 5 condition, and a weight-0 π on PGL₂(𝔸_F) with ρ̄ ≅ r̄_ι(π) matching ordinarity at potentially crystalline places and ι-ordinary and non-potentially-crystalline at the others.

Layers to plan. (1) The topological adelic formalism for completed cohomology at a set S of p-adic places (imported from ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces, extended by the source route of this paper to ALS.3/ALS.6). (2) P-ordinary Hida theory for the Betti cohomology of the unitary spaces X̃_{K̃} at Siegel-parahoric and Q-parahoric levels: Hecke algebras of the monoids Δ̃^Q and their rescaled actions, the P-ordinary functors RΓ(U⁰,−)^{ord}, ord_b, ord₀ and their dual versions, independence of level (Cor. 2.2.9) and of weight (Props. 2.2.15, 2.2.17). This generalises PA.2's Borel-ordinary functor, which it imports and specialises to. (3) The P-ordinary part of a parabolic induction (Prop. 2.3.11, Cor. 2.3.12) via the Bruhat filtration (Hauseux) and Emerton's ordinary parts, and the cohomology of induced spaces (Lemma 2.3.14). (4) The splitting of RΓ(U₀, O/ϖ^m) at deep level (Lemma 2.3.17) and the Artin–Rees subquotient lemma. (5) The Galois side: Q-ordinary automorphic representations have block-triangular Galois representations with crystalline diagonal blocks and determined determinants (Theorem 3.1.2, from Lemma 3.1.3, Newton above Hodge). (6) The completed boundary computation (Theorem 4.1.3, Cor. 4.1.9) and degree shifting at deep auxiliary level (Props. 4.2.2, 4.2.4, 4.2.6, 4.2.8) with the spectral-sequence comparison and descending induction that replace ACC+'s hypothesis p > n², p unramified. (7) Torsion local–global compatibility (Prop. 4.2.13, with its twisting Sub-lemma) and Theorems 4.2.15 and 4.3.1. (8) GL₂/PGL₂ patching with local rings having two components (Assumption 5.4.1, Prop. 5.4.2, Cor. 5.4.3), the special case Prop. 5.6.1 and the solvable base change of Theorem 5.2 (Lemma 5.6.5).

Imports: PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.0–PA.4 (integral cohomology interface, Weyl modules, Borel-ordinary theory, derived support, auxiliary primes; PA.2's Borel-ordinary functor and its maps on parabolic induction are the B-case of layer (2) and are imported, not re-planned); Hida and Coleman families (PadicFamilies L0a, the group-independent ordinary projector); ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.1–ALS.6; IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.7 (Caraiani–Scholze concentration; the paper uses Koshikawa to drop the length-two hypothesis); IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0–IHG.5; TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure TC.2–TC.3; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.2, AG2.5, AG2.7; LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2–R08.4, L7, L8 (with this paper's source items); GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1–R04.5; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P8–P9 and R03.3, R03.6 (components of completed tensor products, [BLGHT11, Lemma 3.3]); IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.7 as widened by this paper's route 7 (Theorem 2.1.28 without the length-two and [F⁺:Q] > 1 hypotheses); GL₂ automorphic representations and transfer (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4) and ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.5 for solvable base change and descent ([ACC+18, Prop. 6.5.13]). The layer (8) also owns Allen–Khare–Thorne's Taylor–Wiles data without enormous image ([AKT23, Prop. A.6]). Lemma 5.6.5 is false as printed when d = 3 and the projective image is A₄ (source issue E12): state it with that exception, and either restrict Theorem 5.2 to exclude p ≡ 1 mod 3 with [F₁(ζ_p):F₁] = 3 and projective image A₄, or supply another argument for the auxiliary places v₀, v₀′ there; the cases p = 3, 5 used by the elliptic-curve Part II are unaffected. Allen–Khare–Thorne (Camb. J. Math. 11, 2023) supplies the PGL₂ cohomology at non-neat level and the Taylor–Wiles and base-change steps; it is a prerequisite paper. Coordinate with the sibling Part IIs of the same parent: WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting (PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25) imports this paper's Theorems 4.2.15 and 4.3.1, Lemma 5.3.3, Proposition 5.4.2 and Corollary 5.4.3, which are owned here; AutomorphyLiftingBeyondTaylorWiles (Calegari–Geraghty) records subsequent work including this local–global compatibility. Hevesi (arXiv:2311.13514) extends Theorem 4.2.15 to the potentially semistable case; plan the crystalline case first and keep the interface open for it. Acceptance tests: n = 2 with λ trivial and p = 3, 5 ramified in F (the case used for elliptic curves); the three parabolic cases; the dual-coefficient degree shifting for q < ⌊d/2⌋.
routes.reason: PA.1 and PA.2 plan local–global compatibility at p only in the Fontaine–Laffaille and Borel-ordinary cases, and nothing in the atlas plans P-ordinary Hida theory for the unitary Betti cohomology, degree shifting at deep auxiliary level, crystalline local–global compatibility for torsion classes, or the potentially Barsotti–Tate lifting theorem over CM fields. A Part II of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure; make_queue folds it with the sibling Part IIs of that parent into DESIGN-PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII (pending). PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 already imports this paper's results into its WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting. Review: accepted. Allen–Khare–Thorne's Taylor–Wiles data were added; the brief now names PA.2 as the imported Borel case, PadicFamilies L0a, R03.3/R03.6, R17.4, ML.5 and route 7, and records the gap E12 in the proof of Theorem 5.2.

routes.title: Modularity and modular parametrisations of elliptic curves over Q, Part II: elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic and CM fields
routes.brief:
Starts where Modularity and modular parametrisations of elliptic curves over Q (EllipticCurveModularity) stops: that roadmap proves modularity over Q; this Part II proves the modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic and imaginary CM fields, following §§6–7 of Caraiani–Newton, 'On the modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields', arXiv:2301.10509v3 (27 March 2025).

Final theorems, as the paper states them. A curve E/F is modular if it has CM or r^∨_{E,p} ≅ r_{π,ι} for a cuspidal regular algebraic π of GL₂(𝔸_F) of weight 0. (a) Theorem 6.1: F imaginary CM with ζ₅ ∉ F; if r̄_{E,3} (resp. r̄_{E,5}) is decomposed generic and absolutely irreducible on G_{F(ζ₃)} (resp. G_{F(ζ₅)}), E is modular. (b) Corollary 6.1.1: for F imaginary quadratic, absolute irreducibility of r̄_{E,3}|_{G_{F(ζ₃)}} or r̄_{E,5}|_{G_{F(ζ₅)}} suffices (Lemma 6.2.2: over quadratic fields this implies decomposed genericity, via Goursat and Chebotarev). (c) Corollary 6.1.2: for F imaginary CM Galois over Q with ζ₅ ∉ F, 100% of Weierstrass equations over F, ordered by height, define modular curves. (d) Theorem 7.1: for F imaginary quadratic, E is modular if G_F acts irreducibly on E[5], or irreducibly on E[3] with image not the normalizer of a split Cartan. (e) Corollary 7.1.2 (Theorem 1.1): if X₀(15)(F) is finite, every E/F is modular.

Layers to plan. (1) Mod-3 and mod-5 switching with prescribed reduction types at p (Props. 6.1.5, 6.1.6, after Allen–Khare–Thorne 9.12–9.15), with Hilbert irreducibility and weak approximation, and the local properties of the auxiliary automorphic representation (Lemmas 6.1.3, 6.1.7, 6.1.4). (2) Theorem 6.1 by applying the potentially Barsotti–Tate lifting theorem of the PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure Part II proposed by this paper (Theorem 5.2), and solvable descent.
